title: Baghel Singh Receives Honors and Proposes a Demonstration

blocks.text: The audience itself is conducted with conspicuous respect. Baghel Singh offered a bow and arrow to the emperor, is invited to sit in front of the king, and watches as his accompanying chiefs are similarly received with ceremony and rank.

From there the court moves into gift-giving and symbolic inclusion. The highest title that belonged to the Muslim royal court is bestowed, along with elephants, drums, jewels, and other marks of distinction meant to display imperial favor.

At parting the emperor asks to witness the famed Sikh manner of looting, and Baghel Singh answers with a controlled spectacle. He directs attention to a field of sugarcane crop across the river (Yamuna), where the requested demonstration will be staged.
